newsitem.title: UK: ED&FMan sees progress at sugar, cocoa units.
newsitem.headline: ED&FMan sees progress at sugar, cocoa units.

text.p: British-based commodities and financial services group E D & F Man Group Plc said on Thursday it expects its sugar business to resume its medium term growth trend and its cocoa operations to return to profitability.

The group reported a five percent increase in pretax profits for the year to March 31 of 85.2 million stg, a figure that had been cut back by 3.4 million stg owing to sterling's strength. It proposed a total dividend of 10.7 pence a share, up six percent.

The molasses business was "considerably strengthened" by the acquisition in February of Cargill's Molasses Liquid Products Division (MLPD), while its "coffee, nuts and spices activities will continue the encouraging progress seen this year," the group said in the results statement.
"Overall, we are confident that the implementation of our strategy of focused investment will deliver growth in earnings and sustain our high returns on capital," it said.
Pretax profits for its sugar business fell to 31.6 million stg from 45.5 million the year before.
"This result masks the continued strong profitability, particularly in North America and Western Europe or our core merchanting business," it said.
Around half the decline was the result of oversupply and sharply reduced local sugar prices in the Former Soviet Union and East European regions.

The molasses and alcohol division saw pretax profits of 10.5 million, down from 11.2 million the year before. An improved contribution from molasses and storage business offset a lower return from other businesses.

The cocoa, coffee, nuts and spices business saw unchanged pretax profits of 4.1 million stg overall. A profit of 8.7 million from coffee, nuts and spices was partially offset by a 4.6 million loss on cocoa.
The cocoa business managed a positive second half contribution before 1.6 million stg of restructuring expenses relating to London and Brazil, the company said.

On the financial services side of the group, Man International showed pretax profits up 13 percent at 12.5 million. "We increased our volume share on major markets and maintained our leading position on several exchanges," the group said.
The Man Investment Products division enjoyed an "outstanding" second half with pretax profits more than doubling to 30.5 million stg from 14.2 million stg previously.
